Subject: Proposal: tailored GPU pool options for Celestis (initial draft)

Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Attached is an initial proposal for a deal-linked GPU pool that maps to the usage profile you shared: a medium-throughput inference service with occasional high-burst periods for batch reprocessing. The attached PDF lays out three footprint options, a recommended minimum-guarantee (min GPUs) per lane, and a staged ramp schedule aimed to balance cost predictability and headroom.

High-level ask: could you confirm which of the three footprints (Compact / Standard / Expanded) best aligns with your Q3 roadmap? Once you pick a lane we can finalize the ramp dates and propose a small SLA uplift for mid-month heavy batching windows.

Quick notes: 
- Compact: 16 min GPUs, burst up to 32 for 6 hours/day during month 1. 
- Standard: 32 min GPUs, burst to 64 with 12-hr burst windows during month 1-2.
- Expanded: 64 baseline with reserved burst headroom and dedicated prewarm lanes.

Attachments: Celestis_GPU_Pool_Proposal_v2.pdf (proposal), SLA_uplift_matrix.xlsx (cost lift table)

Next steps: pick footprint, confirm preferred ramp cadence (monthly vs. bi-weekly), and Procurement folks can route the SOW.

Thanks —
Marissa

Tom / Priya —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers and a recommended ramp + billing model that balances predictability and flexibility. I also attached an internal cost delta matrix to guide the SLA uplift conversation (SLA_uplift_matrix.xlsx).

1) Compact lane MRC and overage behavior
- Min monthly recurring charge (MRC) for Compact is tied to the 16-min GPU guarantee. We propose a flat MRC that covers 16 GPUs at baseline utilization (price detailed in the PDF). Usage above the 16-GPU guarantee is billed as tokenized usage with a tiered burst rate; the first 100GPU-hrs above baseline / month are billed at a discounted burst rate, thereafter at standard on-demand. This hybrid keeps your baseline predictable while capping marginal cost exposure during short bursts.

2) Sustained burst triggers and change control
- If the customer's burst utilization exceeds 20% of days in a 30-day window for two consecutive months, we trigger a "sustained-burst review". Outcomes: (a) suggest moving to Standard lane (32 min GPUs) with prorated MRC/credits, (b) enable a temporary burst-extension for up to 30 days with a one-time activation fee, or (c) keep Compact and apply a dynamic burst surcharge. No punitive decommit; we use credits/prorate to make transitions smooth.

3) Onboarding / warm-start credits
- Standard one-time onboarding credit: equivalent to 10% of month-1 MRC applied as platform credits to offset initial warm-up costs. If customer signs for >12 months we can increase to 20% as an incentive. For Compact->Standard mid-contract transitions, we offer partial onboarding credits toward the Standard activation.

4) Instance-level mapping and network planning
- Compact: 16 GPUs = 2 racks of 8xA500 (or 1 rack of 8xA100 + flex vCPU headroom depending on performance profile).
- Standard: 32 GPUs = 4xA500 or 2xA100 equivalent racks.
- Expanded: suggested layout is 8xA500 + pre-warmed lane instances to guarantee low cold-start latency.

5) Recommended ramp schedule (decision-ready)
- Week 0: Contract sign + SOW + activation window scheduling (2 weeks prep).
- Month 1: Compact baseline active (16 min GPUs) with configured 6-12 hr burst windows.
- Month 2: Evaluate burst metrics; if sustained-burst review conditions met, propose move to Standard with 7-day notice and prorated MRC changes in Month 3.
- Month 3-6: Stabilize and optionally enable reserved prewarm lanes for Scheduled batch windows (additional cost in SLA uplift matrix).

Other notes: we can include a 30-day grace period for downscales to avoid churn during early experimentation. I added the HubSpot deal link in the attachment header for Marissa to update pricing terms: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deals/9341

If this looks good I can draft the technical appendix for the SOW (instance sku table, network egress guidance, and prewarm runbook).

—Karthik
